classification.difficultyReason: Implement equal-chance digit sampling, convert sample even counts to proportions, plot repeated results and compare larger samples using the taught variability model.

inlines.text: You know that the digits 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 are the even digits and 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 are the odd digits.
We know that 50% of digits are even.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Randomly select 20 digits. This can be done by using a calculator or computer or by having a bucket full of pieces of paper with a digit on each. Of course, there must be the same number of occurrences of each digit.

answer.worked: Answers vary. Use a random digit generator with digits 0–9 equally likely, and record 20 selections. One possible result is 7, 2, 0, 9, 4, 1, 6, 3, 8, 5, 2, 7, 4, 9, 0, 1, 8, 3, 6, 5. This sample contains 10 even digits.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Compare your results with others and record all of the results on a dot plot. For each sample, calculate the proportion of digits that are even and plot that sample proportion.

answer.short: Answers vary. Sample proportions from six samples might be 40%, 45%, 50%, 50%, 55% and 60%; place one dot for each sample.
answer.worked:
For the sample in part a:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Proportion even}&=\frac{10}{20}\\\text{Proportion even}&=0.5=50\%\end{align*}$$
Calculate the proportion even for each person's sample. For example, counts of 8, 9, 10, 10, 11 and 12 even digits out of 20 give 40%, 45%, 50%, 50%, 55% and 60%. Plot each sample proportion once, stacking dots for repeated values.

spec.description: Authored example dot plot of six sample proportions; no graph is supplied in the source.
spec.mathematics: One dot at 40%, 45%, 55% and 60%; two dots at 50%.

answer.short: Answers vary. Larger samples usually give proportions closer to 50%, with less variation between samples.
answer.worked: Repeat the random selection using larger samples and calculate the proportion even for each sample. For example, samples of 100 digits containing 47, 49, 50, 51 and 53 even digits give 47%, 49%, 50%, 51% and 53%. Record and compare the results using a dot plot. Larger samples generally show less variation around 50%; an individual larger sample is not guaranteed to be closer.
